gen-gf-grandstander-gf-alumni-sans-pinst: Bold and loud would be wrong; expressive fits Grandstander's open-handed letters and tall x-height, while Alumni Sans Pinstripe tucks in beside it with oversized lowercase. Its hairline strokes are the pair's boldest surprise.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Alumni Sans SC reads tight and tall, its lowercase towering over its own capitals. Grandstander's pen-like line holds one width, so the two trade a blunt stroke for a faintly shaded one.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-anaheim: Grandstander draws every stroke like a plotter pen, one width from start to finish, with short ascenders. Anaheim follows in rounded, densely packed sans-serif forms, and the eye glides through them while the heading stays loud.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-arsenal: Arsenal keeps its lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals, with a close-knit run of letters and a mild weight shift in each stroke. Grandstander's dowel-straight stems are the louder voice; Arsenal's quiet shading is the steadier one.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-arsenal-sc: Every Grandstander stroke is traced at the width of one stylus. Arsenal SC adds a faint thick-thin shift and tight fit, so a long passage would move smoothly, with no harsh thin spots to snag on.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-asimovian: Grandstander's stems are plain and constant in width, with letters held open and short ascenders over a tall x-height. Asimovian echoes that single stroke width, and that shared construction is what ties them.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-basic: Expressive is the first word for Grandstander, whose lines keep a single unbroken weight from terminals to junctions. Basic follows with a sans that bumps only gently from small letters up to capitals.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-cal-sans: Cal Sans takes the body role with one stroke width running through its whole alphabet, tall x-height included. Grandstander is the one built to announce, while Cal Sans keeps its sans lines moving underneath.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-carlito: Loud, round, and thread-like: Grandstander's single line is easy to follow. Carlito answers in sans-serif that sits snug, like thread on a spool, with big lowercase and smaller-looking capitals.
gen-gf-grandstander-gf-changa: Grandstander builds even its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, and that bold, expressive confidence carries every word. Make the heading small and Changa's cast-iron lowercase would start to outshout it.
